newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end with strong recovery.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end with strong recovery.

text.p: Swiss shares ended with an strong recovery of one percent after a sharp slump on Wednesday.
"We had a surprising rally," one dealer said, citing short covering, firmer bonds and the U.S. dollar as well as a reaction to Wednesday's "exaggerated" losses.
Initial caution due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S. and rumours of Roche takeover plans was brushed aside.
One dealer warned fears of a correction on Wall Street persist, adding the market may move sideways.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 38.8 points, or 1.01 percent, to 3,884.1 points.
Dealers said banks made a comeback after being under heavy pressure following UBS's Tuesday announcement of an extraordinary charge that will cause a 1996 loss of 500 million Swiss francs.
CS Holding jumped 2.8 percent to 136.50 francs in moderate volumes. UBS bearer shares added 12 francs to 1,223.
Rumours that Roche was mulling a takeover of Smithkline or Astra had little impact. "Initially, it caused a stir, but nobody could really believe it", he said.
Another trader said the rumours were "just rubbish". Roche declined to comment.
Roche ended up 95 francs to 9,925 after a massive slump on Wednesday.
Insurer Winterthur soared 1.4 percent to 796 francs. A dealer said the stock had lagged behind the market recently.
Among industrials, Ciba, Sandoz, Alusuisse, Holderbank and Electrowatt ended more than one percent higher.
Alusuisse, which climbed 18 francs to 1,035, was said to profit from of a presentation in London and rumours of a positive study.
Adecco and Swissair lost around 0.3 percent each.
